headline: High-risk shared-server workflow: n8n’s server-side execution and broad egress can cascade into unsafe actions when paired with plano’s OpenAI-compatible gateway and logs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow inputs and execute server-side tools, while plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and handles logs/metrics. If n8n passes untrusted content into plano and then reuses the response, prompt injection can cross the pair. No shared channel is explicit, so this is not high.
conditions: IF n8n workflows forward untrusted text into plano chat completions
IF plano responses are later treated as instructions by n8n without filtering
mitigations: Add an allowlist prompt template in n8n
Strip tool instructions from plano outputs before reuse
Insert a human review step for first-run workflows
Log and alert on unexpected instruction-like tokens
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and writes to the server filesystem; plano touches traces, metrics, and logs and calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If n8n sends workflow data into plano, sensitive content can leak into logs or third-party inference. The pair lacks explicit isolation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF workflow inputs include secrets, customer data, or regulated records
IF n8n forwards those inputs to plano or plano logs them
mitigations: Redact secrets before sending data to plano
Disable verbose request/response logging
Use a test dataset for initial integration
Restrict n8n credentials to least privilege
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive workflows from the gateway

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and broad network egress; plano has broad network egress and a config file surface. They can both mutate shared external resources through APIs, creating overlapping write-like effects even without direct filesystem contention. Uncertainty about the exact shared resource pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same API-backed resource or credential store
IF n8n workflows and plano routing rules are edited concurrently
mitigations: Separate credentials per agent
Freeze config changes during rollout
Add a simple change log for shared resources
Run one agent in read-only mode for validation
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates tools, so it can act on upstream outputs; plano is an AI gateway that can route or relay model outputs. If n8n consumes plano output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or bad automations. Because the pair can default into action-taking without verification, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF n8n uses plano output as a decision input
IF no verification or approval step is inserted before tool execution
mitigations: Require a confirmation step before side effects
Compare plano output against a second source
Limit n8n tools to dry-run mode initially
Add schema validation on routed outputs
requires-engineering: implement policy checks before execution

E_compliance.rationale: n8n can process whatever the workflow processes and stores secrets on its server; plano explicitly handles traces, metrics, and logs. If regulated data flows through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are routed through both agents
IF their logging or retention settings differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to plano
Set short log retention on both systems
Document data categories allowed in each workflow
Purge test logs after validation
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
